summary: The source permits at most 100 elements, which is too narrow for honest runtime scaling, while filtering an arbitrary array has a matching linear worst-case lower bound.

optimality.argument: When the target is absent, a correct algorithm must inspect every one of the n values to establish that all n belong in the retained prefix, giving an Omega(n) worst-case lower bound. The stable compaction implementation reads each value once and performs at most one constant-time write for it, so its upper bound is O(n).

replacement_checks.evidence: For an arbitrary unsorted array, any unread position could contain the target and change both the returned count and required retained multiset.
The current implementation performs one forward scan, advances the write boundary only for retained values, and carries only fixed scalar state.

Regression exhausts all arrays through length six over a representative value alphabet and all target-presence modes, then checks every legal length through 100 with boundary targets against both app-local and immutable native sources.
